concepts.def: Life is sacred and God-given; Christian (Genesis 1:27); Islamic (Qur'an 17:33); foundation of pro-life ethics.
Catholic absolute prohibition; Anglican case-by-case; Islam permits before 120 days (ensoulment); Buddhist generally opposes.
Active (lethal injection) vs passive (withdrawing treatment); Christianity opposes active; doctrine of double effect permits pain relief.
Christianity: eternal communion with God or separation; Islam: Jannah (Paradise) or Jahannam (Hell); judgement based on deeds and faith.
Hindu, Buddhist, Sikh belief in rebirth based on karma; aim is liberation (moksha, nibbana, mukti) from cycle.
Spiritual essence; Christianity created by God; Hindu atman eternal; Buddhism rejects fixed self (anatta).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Theme B: Religion & Life — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Theme B: Religion & Life brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Theme B: Religion & Life.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: At what day does Islam consider ensoulment?

numericals.q: After how many days does Islam consider ensoulment?

free_texts.q: Name the Hindu term for eternal soul.
free_texts.hint: Identical with Brahman in Advaita Vedanta.
